# control-anything

> Control theory as an instrument for judging AI systems. Every claim carries a guarantee
> level (G0 anecdote → G4 certified) and an assumption ledger; a gate mechanically caps the
> guarantee at what those assumptions actually discharge. "We used an MPC, therefore it is
> safe" is a failing exit code here.

## Core idea
A control claim is worth exactly the weakest assumption holding it up.
effective = min(claimed, weakest-assumption-ceiling, best-evidence-ceiling)
An `assumed` assumption ceilings a claim at G1; `monitored` at G3; `violated` refuses it.

## The six organs
Every feedback loop has: reference, comparator, controller, actuator, plant, sensor —
plus latency, authority and fallback, which is where real systems fail. A thermostat, a
humanoid and an LLM agent differ in what FILLS each slot, never in which slots exist.

## Key files
- GOAL.md — the 10x contract; §0 evaluates the request before anything else
- data/claims.yml — the claim corpus the gate judges
- data/loops.yml — twelve LoopCards, one per domain
- data/applications.yml — 34 deployed control loops and the guarantee each actually claims
- data/works.yml — 86 works; `bridge: rigorous|analogy` separates theorems from metaphors
- src/control_anything/core/claim_gate.py — the gate
- src/control_anything/core/models.py — the guarantee ladder and the six organs

## Commands
make check                     # the whole gate: offline, deterministic, ~2s
python3 scripts/ca.py stats    # the metrics
python3 scripts/ca.py gate     # judge every claim
python3 scripts/ca.py loopify <system>
python3 scripts/ca.py trace <claim-id>

## Honest edges
The G0-G4 ladder is a design judgement, not a theorem. unverified_rate is 0.53 and is
published rather than hidden. Nothing here runs a live plant.
